messages.name: lookup_refund_policy
messages.content: {"ok": true, "sections": [{"citation": "refund-policy/v2/window", "title": "Time limit", "text": "A refund must be requested no later than 30 days after the delivery time recorded on the order. Days are exact periods of twenty-four hours, and a request at exactly the deadline is on time. The request time is the moment the shop creates the refund proposal. If an earlier proposal for the same units was created in time and then expired, or stopped being valid because the order or this policy changed, before it was paid, a later request for those units is not refused for being late: a staff member takes the case. A proposal that the customer replaced or cancelled, that a staff member rejected, or that a handoff closed does not count. A request for an exception to the time limit is refused with this reason."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/eligible-orders", "title": "Which orders qualify", "text": "Only orders with the status \"delivered\" can receive a refund. An order that has not been delivered is not refunded through this process: the assistant tells the customer the order's status, and cancelling the order or changing its delivery is outside this process, so the assistant offers a staff member for that. If an order is recorded as delivered but the customer says it never arrived, a staff member takes the case. If a delivered order has no delivery time, or one that cannot be right (before the purchase or in the future), a staff member takes the case."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/payment", "title": "Where the money goes", "text": "A refund is paid automatically only when the order has exactly one payment record and that record is valid (a known payment method and a positive amount), and only to that payment. Instalments of one payment are one payment record. When the order has several payment records, or its one record is not valid, a staff member takes the case. A refund can never be sent to another person, account or card: such a request is refused with this reason, and the refund can still go to the original payment if the customer accepts. A customer's statement that the original card was cancelled does not change where the refund goes; the card's issuer handles the credit, and the shop cannot promise where or when it appears."}], "note": "Cite a section by its citation ID, exactly as given."}
